newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa scraps cargo fuel surcharge from APRIL 15.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa scraps cargo fuel surcharge from APRIL 15.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it is dropping its 10 US cents per kg air cargo fuel surcharge with effect from April 15.
Fuel prices had now returned to the levels of July 1996 and the surcharge could now be lifted, a Lufthansa Cargo statement said.
"In dropping the surcharge Lufthansa Cargo is honouring the commitment it gave last November to scrap it again once fuel prices fell to the level of July 1996," the statement said.
"Experience has shown that a renewed rise in jet fuel prices is not normally to be expected in the summer months," it added.
Delta Air Lines was the first airline to drop the surcharge on March 13 and United Airlines and Virgin Atlantic Cargo have since followed.
Lufthansa Cargo first introduced a surcharge of 15 pfennigs per kg, then roughly equivalent to 10 US cents, on November 1 at three days' notice.
The move was rapidly followed by airlines in most world air cargo markets.
A similar surcharge was later added to passenger fares by most airlines in the International Air Transport Association (IATA).
But pressure has been growing from air cargo shippers and freight forwarders on airlines to drop the surcharge in recent weeks.

On April 3, the European Air Shippers Council (EASC) called on airlines to scrap the surcharge on the grounds it could no longer be justified. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax+5017
